name: Custom HLDS game
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Any game or mod on Valve's Half-Life engine, such as Counter-Strike 1.6, Day of Defeat or Team Fortress Classic. Installs the Half-Life dedicated server with SteamCMD and keeps it updated, with ReHLDS if you want it.
startup: if [ "{{AUTO_UPDATE}}" = 1 ]; then ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /home/container +login anonymous +app_set_config 90 mod {{HLDS_GAME}} +app_update {{SRCDS_APPID}} ${SRCDS_BETAID:+-beta "$SRCDS_BETAID"} ${SRCDS_BETAPASS:+-betapassword "$SRCDS_BETAPASS"} $([ "{{VALIDATE}}" = 1 ] && echo validate) +quit || echo "Steam couldn't update the game, so the server starts as it is."; fi; [ "{{REHLDS}}" = 1 ] && [ -d .raptor-rehlds ] && cp -rf .raptor-rehlds/. .; exec ./hlds_run -console -game {{HLDS_GAME}} -port {{SERVER_PORT}} -sport {{VAC_PORT}} -strictportbind -norestart +ip 0.0.0.0 +maxplayers {{MAX_PLAYERS}} +map {{SRCDS_MAP}} +hostname "{{SERVER_NAME}}"

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Half-Life engine games. Installs or updates the dedicated server (Steam app 90) with
# SteamCMD, signed in anonymously, with the game chosen in Game and
# ReHLDS when asked. Maps, configs and plugins are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
export HOME=/mnt/server
app="${SRCDS_APPID:-90}"
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

# SteamCMD stays in the server folder, so the server can update itself at start.
if [ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]; then
    echo "Downloading SteamCMD"
    mkdir -p steamcmd
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz | tar -xz -C steamcmd
fi
mkdir -p steamapps
args=(+force_install_dir /mnt/server +login anonymous +app_set_config 90 mod "${HLDS_GAME:-cstrike}" +app_update "$app")
[ -z "${SRCDS_BETAID:-}" ] || args+=(-beta "$SRCDS_BETAID")
[ -z "${SRCDS_BETAPASS:-}" ] || args+=(-betapassword "$SRCDS_BETAPASS")
[ "${VALIDATE:-0}" != 1 ] || args+=(validate)
# SteamCMD often fails once for no lasting reason (Missing configuration,
# state 0x202 or 0x602 after it updates itself): try again, up to 5 times.
for try in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "${args[@]}" +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log || true
    grep -aq "Success! App '$app'" /tmp/steamcmd.log && [ -f "${HLDS_GAME:-cstrike}/liblist.gam" ] && break
    err=$(grep -aE '^(ERROR|Error)!' /tmp/steamcmd.log | tail -n 1) || true
    case "$err" in
    *"No subscription"*) fail "Steam won't give this game to an anonymous account, so it can't be installed." ;;
    *"Invalid Password"* | *"Invalid beta"*) fail "Steam refused the beta branch or its password. Check Beta branch and Beta password, then reinstall." ;;
    esac
    [ "$try" = 5 ] && fail "SteamCMD failed 5 times (${err:-no error given}). If it mentions 0x202, the server may be out of disk space. Reinstall to try again."
    echo "SteamCMD failed; trying again ($((try + 1)) of 5)."
    sleep 5
done
# Steam's client library, where the game looks for it.
mkdir -p .steam/sdk32 .steam/sdk64
cp -f steamcmd/linux32/steamclient.so .steam/sdk32/
cp -f steamcmd/linux64/steamclient.so .steam/sdk64/
build=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*"buildid"[[:space:]]*"\([0-9]*\)".*/\1/p' "steamapps/appmanifest_$app.acf" | head -n 1)

# ReHLDS, the reverse-engineered engine, when asked. Its files are kept in
# .raptor-rehlds, so the server can put them back after Steam updates HLDS.
extra=""
if [ "${REHLDS:-0}" = 1 ]; then
    repo=rehlds/ReHLDS
    want="${VERSION:-latest}"
    if ! tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$want" 2>/dev/null); then
        [ "$want" = latest ] && fail "GitHub can't be reached right now to download ReHLDS. Reinstall to try again."
        fail "ReHLDS has no version $want. Set ReHLDS version to latest, or to one of its releases, such as $(gh-release tag "$repo" latest 2>/dev/null || echo 3.15.0.896)."
    fi
    if [ -d .raptor-rehlds ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-rehlds.version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
        echo "ReHLDS $tag is already downloaded."
    else
        echo "Downloading ReHLDS $tag"
        work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
        rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
        trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
        gh-release download "$repo" "$tag" "rehlds-bin-$tag.zip" "$work/rehlds.zip" || fail "ReHLDS $tag has no server download, or it failed. Choose another version, or reinstall to try again."
        unzip -q "$work/rehlds.zip" 'bin/linux32/*' -d "$work" || fail "The ReHLDS download is damaged. Reinstall to try again."
        rm -rf .raptor-rehlds
        mv "$work/bin/linux32" .raptor-rehlds
        echo "$tag" > .raptor-rehlds.version
    fi
    cp -rf .raptor-rehlds/. .
    extra=" with ReHLDS $tag"
elif [ -d .raptor-rehlds ]; then
    echo "Putting Valve's engine back, as ReHLDS is off."
    ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "${args[@]}" validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log || true
    grep -aq "Success! App '$app'" /tmp/steamcmd.log || fail "SteamCMD couldn't put the game's own files back. Reinstall to try again."
    rm -rf .raptor-rehlds .raptor-rehlds.version
fi
echo "Installed HLDS build ${build:-unknown} for ${HLDS_GAME:-cstrike}${extra}${SRCDS_BETAID:+ from the $SRCDS_BETAID branch}."

variables.name: Game
variables.description: The game's folder name, such as cstrike, czero, dod, tfc, gearbox, ricochet or valve. Reinstall after changing it.

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: The name players see in the server browser.

variables.name: Map
variables.description: The map the server starts on; it must be one of the game's, such as de_dust2 for cstrike or crossfire for valve.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: How many players can be on the server at once.

variables.name: ReHLDS
variables.description: Run ReHLDS, a faster engine that's compatible with Valve's, instead of Valve's own. Reinstall after changing it.

variables.name: ReHLDS version
variables.description: The ReHLDS release to install, such as 3.14.0.857, or latest.

variables.name: Auto update
variables.description: Update the game from Steam every time the server starts.

variables.name: Validate files
variables.description: Check every game file against Steam when installing or updating, which repairs damaged files but takes longer.

variables.name: Beta branch
variables.description: The Steam beta branch to install, or empty for the normal release. Reinstall after changing it.

variables.name: Beta password
variables.description: The password of a private beta branch, if it has one.

variables.name: Steam app ID
variables.description: The dedicated server's Steam app ID, which SteamCMD installs.
